packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-07 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING (first reader)

EXPOSURE / RULES STATEMENT
Nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification of a work or author before or during this reading.
Visible inside the images themselves (not from any outside context): a round ink stamp reading "ÖSTERR. NATIONALBIBLIOTHEK WIEN" and a modern pencil note "Fragm. 127" at the lower left of the written face (image-001, image-008), with a pencil "1" at the top left (image-002). I report these as things seen on the leaf.
Beyond the stated rules I did one thing: I listed the file names of the packet directory itself (to learn how many image files there were). That listing showed the name "packet.json"; I did not open it. I opened only PROMPT.md and image-001.jpg to image-018.jpg. No web, search, catalogue or edition was used.

1. LAYOUT SURVEY (observations)
- Two faces. image-001.jpg is the overview of the written face; image-002 to image-009 are its overlapping native-resolution tiles (two across, four down: 002/003 top, 004/005, 006/007, 008/009 bottom). image-010.jpg is the overview of the other face; image-011 to image-018 are its tiles.
- The other face (image-010 to image-018) carries NO writing of its own that I can see. What is visible there is the mirror-image show-through of the written face (the same hole, the same line pattern reversed), plus the reversed ghost of the stamp and pencil shelfmark at lower right (image-018) and a small "x"/cross mark. I transcribe nothing from it.
- Written face: upright, single block of long lines, widely spaced (about 25-26 lines), in a cursive documentary-looking hand with long descenders and looped ascenders. No columns, no running title, no rubric, no enlarged or decorated initial, no underlining, no interlinear or marginal gloss. Brown ink, very faded in the lower third; a reddish stain in the middle; an oval hole right of centre (image-005/007); the top edge is torn with a large loss at top centre that removes the middle of lines 1-3; the lower left is abraded.
- The last line is short and ends with the word "appenso", after which the parchment is blank. A small cross-like mark stands below the text at lower left (image-008 line 6).
- Tentative interpretation (not an identification of a work): the wording is that of a legal/administrative instrument rather than a book text - a letter by which someone, on a presentation by a holder of a right of patronage, institutes and invests a named cleric in a church and orders that he be led into corporal possession, closing with a sealing clause. This rests on the phrases read below (Jus patronatus, Instituimus, auctoritate ordinaria, per libri tradicionem, corporalem possessionem vel quasi pacificam et quietam, inducatis, appenso).

2. AREAS SELECTED / UNREAD
I read the whole written face line by line as far as I could, since it is short. Weakest areas: line 1 (almost wholly lost), the middles of lines 2-4 (hole), lines 9-11 (stain and cockling), and lines 20-26 (faded/abraded). The show-through face is left unread on purpose.

3. TRANSCRIPTION, WRITTEN FACE
Conventions: ( ) proposed expansion; (?) after a word = uncertain reading; [illegible] = unreadable; [hole]/[lost] = physical loss. Each physical line of the leaf is given once per tile; the left and right tiles of a pair show the same physical lines and overlap in the middle, so text repeated between them is NOT additional text. Vertically adjacent tiles also overlap by about one line.

4. CONNECTED READING OF THE BEST SPAN (assembled from the paired tiles; same uncertainties apply)
Physical lines 12-19 of the face, counting the lost first line as 1:
... Inueſtim(us)(?) ... et Inſtituim(us) auct(oritat)e ordinaria nob(is)(?) ... /
... p(er)mitt...(?) p(er) libri t(ra)dicionem ... /
... eſt Inueſtit(us)(?) Delato ſibi p(ri)us(?) [hole] fidel... /
... p(re)ſtit..(?) corp(or)al(i) Juramento(?) [hole] Qu... /
... p(re)ſb(ite)ro(?) ſt(ri)cte(?) ... et(?) Mandam(us) q(ua)t(enu)s ip(su)m ... /
... ad(?) eandem Ecc(lesi)am(?) p(re)notata(m)(?) et Inueſtitu(m) i(n) corp- /
-ralem poſſeſſionem vel quaſi pacificam et quieta(m) Indu... /
... p(re)miſſ.. mittatis(?) et inducatis ſibi ta... /
... et ad q(uo)s p(er)tinet de Vniu(er)[sis] / fructib(us)(?) reddit(ibus)(?) ... o(mn)ib(us) Jurib(us) et obuenc(ionibus)(?) ...

Most secure words on the face: "D(omi)no sempiternam", "D(omi)n(u)m henricu(m) de" + surname (three times: lines 3?, 6, 8), "Jus pat(ro)nat(us)", "Inſtituim(us)", "auct(oritat)e ordinaria", "p(er) libri t(ra)dicionem", "corp(or)al(i) Jurament-", "Mandam(us) q(ua)t(enu)s ip(su)m", "poſſeſſionem vel quaſi pacificam et quieta(m)", "inducatis ſibi", "et ad q(uo)s p(er)tinet", "appenſo".

5. LIMITATIONS
- Line 1 and the centres of lines 2-4 are physically lost; the right ends of most lines run to the trimmed edge and some may be clipped.
- Lines 20-26 are badly faded; I could only pick out isolated words there. The date and sealing clause presumably sit in these lines but I could not read a date, and I have not supplied one.
- Proper names are the least secure readings: the surname after "henricum de" and the place-name after "in" (line 4) are given as letter-shapes, not as resolved names.
- The other face shows only mirror-image show-through; if any endorsement exists there it is not visible in these images.
- A raking-light or contrast-enhanced image of the lower third of the written face would be the most useful addition.
